newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says not decided to stop buying debentures.
newsitem.headline: MOF says not decided to stop buying debentures.

text.p: The Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau has made no changes in its investment plans, and has not decided to stop buying bank debentures, a ministry official said on Wednesday.
"We have not decided to stop buying bank debentures," an official for the Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau told Reuters.

"The Finance Ministry has not changed its thinking regarding the Trust Fund Bureau's purchases of bank debentures, nor have there been any new announcements (regarding investment plans)," the official said.
The official was responding to questions after a domestic financial daily reported on Wednesday that the bureau had not bought bank debentures since April.

The official said the Trust Fund Bureau is under no obligation to buy a set amount of bank debentures each month, and added that investment activity by the bureau tended to slow down at the beginning of the fiscal year, as fund inflows tend to dwindle due to seasonal factors.
The only new recent development has been that the bureau has been able to hold the long-term JGBs it buys regularly from the secondary market until maturity, the official said.
"We now have more ways to make medium-term investments," he said.

In March, a plan by the Trust Fund Bureau to buy 2.4 trillion yen worth of long-term JGBs in fiscal 1997/98 was approved by parliament, enabling the bureau to hold long-term JGBs for five years and longer.
Until March 31, the bureau was allowed to hold long-term JGBs only for a period of up to five years.
The Trust Fund Bureau's funds totalled 388.38 trillion yen as of the end of December 1996, of which bank debentures totalled 9.946 trillion yen.
